long_biography.plain_text:
Born into one of colonial Hong Kong's best-known trading families, Marden studied Chinese and politics at Leeds University. He returned to a maritime tradition established by his grandfather and father. When Wheelock Marden was sold in 1985, he retained and continued the family's shipping interest rather than following the conglomerate into new ownership. Fenwick Shipping became his principal operating platform, specialising in dry-bulk vessels and related services across Hong Kong and Australia.

FIM extended the maritime platform into container shipping, logistics, ship management, bunkering, repairs and consultancy. Marden also became vice-chairman of Lorenzo Shipping and a director of National Marine Corporation. He pursued a separate CleanOil venture that applied closed-loop technology to used-oil re-refining in Zhuhai. The combination shows a family-shaped shipping platform sustained through decades of personal operation and selective expansion into logistics and marine-adjacent environmental technology.
